stepNotes.1: The seven inspection tools are registered across local and full profiles, with LSP separately feature-gated.
stepNotes.2: Filesystem calls resolve NUL-safe paths through external-directory and symlink controls, while Exa calls require network isolation and query-scoped permission.
stepNotes.3: Read handles directory, attachment, binary, and streamed-text branches with explicit pagination; list is abortable and bounded but misses nested built-in ignore directories.
stepNotes.4: Native search payloads are schema-checked and truncation uses a one-record sentinel; grep's native path lacks the fallback mtime ordering promised by its description.
stepNotes.5: LSP validates operation-specific arguments, uses cache-before-live semantics where supported, preserves provenance envelopes, and records audit outcomes.
stepNotes.6: Result counts, bytes, lines, subprocess duration, Exa response size, and best-effort LSP warmup are all explicitly constrained.
stepNotes.7: Shared path, external-access, and Exa helpers centralize policy; exceptional fallbacks either log, preserve the original failure, or have a documented optimization-only role.
stepNotes.8: Focused coverage spans native parsers, permissions, symlinks, truncation, attachments, audit rows, and warmup behavior; no Critical finding exists.
stepNotes.9: Eight focused files passed 91 tests and the core package typecheck passed without any source modification.
